sibling_registration.scope: Same title and named creators in IEEE DataPort; treated as a related registration, not a second experiment. Payload equivalence not checked.

queries: Opened Zenodo record and checked the IEEE DataPort DOI returned by DataCite. Inspected the archive, README, methods for the location labels, and dataset illustration.

Exact associated paper title search via Crossref; DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2022.3201645. IEEE link served HTML rather than PDF and the historical Figshare file URL for the TechRxiv preprint returned 404 in this retrieval. Quantitative claims above use the deposited source files.

article.title: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Contact Tracing Without User Intervention
article.level: publisher metadata, linked by the data deposit

evidence: Full data-file validation: all seven headerless numeric tables across four campaign folders, all four per-folder field descriptions, and archive-level documentation. Router-side eight AP FTM features; six files also have RSSI, and EOW3rdFloorDay1 includes a training file only. Authors describe Chrony on routers, LiDAR/RGB-D location reference and position-local relative time.
findings: 207,541 rows comprise 257 distinct-position blocks across the seven source files. Every one of the 250 within-file position transitions resets relative time backwards. Across the 207,284 within-position adjacent pairs, 155,516 times advance exactly 10 ms and 38,370 exactly 20 ms. In 67 pairs all eight FTM features repeat. This is a processed table without per-AP event clocks, matched packet IDs or sender denominators: local-grid frequency cannot be used as the physical packet delivery rate.

Three campaign folders supply train and test, covering 14+35+33=82 test positions. One of the 35 Day 2 EOW3 test coordinates also occurs in training at the two-decimal precision supplied. The other two matched spatial splits have zero exact coincidences. Repetition of a rounded coordinate does not establish session identity.

For each position, use the per-channel median FTM. Normalize feature differences by each channel’s interquartile range across training positions. Use the nearest training fingerprint to predict the test location (one vote per held-out position). Median physical location errors were 2.067 m ECS1, 0.764 m EOW3 Day2, 1.231 m EOW5. Median nearest available training coordinate distances were 0.704, 0.455 and 0.711 m, respectively. These are descriptive geometry/fingerprint checks under the original folder split, not reproduction of the paper’s BiLSTM.
limitations: Source describes RTT values in nanoseconds but files lack per-transaction timestamps or independent calibration and no passive client-side observations were supplied. Retain values in their source numeric scale. Only router-side measured, processed feature vectors available. Evaluation uses x,y in matched maps, no cross-floor coordinate comparison. The numbers of positions are summed per file and are not counts of distinct subjects or globally distinct coordinates. No individual identities used.
